title: Pixel lock-screen completion lost security-state binding
product: Google Pixel / Android lock-screen state management
summary: A researcher-published vendor decision documents a USD 70,000 award for CVE-2022-20465.
root_cause: The researcher’s patch analysis attributes the issue to completion events dismissing a different active security challenge after concurrent state changes.
impact: Physical access could bypass the lock screen on tested Pixel 5 and 6 devices. Broader Android coverage was not established by the researcher.
defensive_takeaways: Bind authentication completion to the exact challenge and security context it satisfies.
Model concurrent authentication-state transitions and reject stale completion events.
Distinguish a security patch-level label from the date an update reached devices.

reward.evidence_quote: we are happy to reward you the full amount of $70,000 USD
reward.notes: Explicit USD decision for this report. It was initially marked duplicate; the reproduced response explains an exception because the report enabled remediation. Cash receipt is not separately documented.

public_disclosure.note: CVE record publication. The Android bulletin is dated November 7; its original snapshot was not retrieved, so first appearance of this entry is not asserted.

fixed.note: Reported fixed in the November update. The 2022-11-05 patch-level label is not used as an exact rollout date.

recency.note: Historical primary publication outside the preferred last-12-month window.

verification.method: Read the researcher article, full reproduced report discussion and vendor bulletins; checked the explicit award decision and unique CVE. Cross-checked the Google-authored CNA record publication date.
limitations: The award decision is reproduced by the researcher, not independently published by the vendor.
Vendor patch-level labels and bulletin publication dates do not establish each device’s update deployment date.
